canonical_statement: For the nonlinear wave-system class and data spaces specified by the selected primary-source theorem in 3+1-dimensional Minkowski space, sufficiently small smooth initial data satisfying its localization or decay hypotheses admit the asserted global classical solution when the quadratic nonlinearity satisfies Klainerman's null condition.
domain_and_universes: Provisional scope: real-valued finite systems on 3+1-dimensional Minkowski spacetime; exact index types, function spaces, and Lean universes remain open.
quantifiers: a nonlinear wave system in the source theorem's equation class
initial data in the source theorem's smoothness and localization/decay class
data size below a source-dependent positive threshold
hypotheses: source-stated structural assumptions on the nonlinearity
the quadratic part satisfies the source's null condition
data satisfy source-stated compatibility, regularity, localization/decay, and smallness hypotheses
conclusion: Existence, and only if source-stated uniqueness and regularity, of a global classical solution on the source theorem's time domain.
excluded_claims: all equations informally described as satisfying a null condition
boundary_cases: Zero data and vanishing nonlinearity are diagnostic cases, not evidence for the nonlinear root. Removing the null condition is a later mutation probe.
